description: We don't want to build just another weather app. We want to explore how NASA data can become useful intelligence for people living and working on the ocean.
summary:
SEA//SAFE is a location-aware Coastal Environmental Intelligence Platform that transforms satellite-based Earth observation data into accessible, scientifically supported coastal insights.

Initially focusing on Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, the platform uses NASA/JPL PO.DAAC MUR Sea Surface Temperature (SST) v4.1 to analyze historical ocean conditions, seasonal variations, temperature anomalies, and long-term trends.

Users can explore coastal locations through interactive maps, manual search, or optional GPS access. The system processes historical SST data (2003–2025), generates 5 km, 10 km, and 20 km offshore analysis zones, and applies geospatial masking to exclude land pixels.

Scientific methods, including climatology, Theil–Sen slope estimation, and Mann–Kendall trend testing, help identify ocean temperature changes and their statistical significance.

Built using Next.js, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, Xarray, GeoPandas, and MapLibre, SEA//SAFE combines data engineering, scientific computing, geospatial analysis, and interactive visualization.

The platform prioritizes scientific transparency through dataset provenance, methodology, data coverage, and uncertainty. It distinguishes historical observations and statistical trends from validated forecasts, avoiding unsupported predictions.

Its goal is to make oceanographic information accessible to coastal communities, fishers, researchers, educators, and environmental planners.
details:
SEA//SAFE

Coastal Environmental Intelligence Platform

Tagline: See the change. Understand the ocean. Prepare for what comes next.

Initial Pilot: Thiruvananthapuram District, Kerala, India
Primary Dataset: NASA/JPL MUR SST v4.1
Project Type: Environmental Intelligence & Geospatial Analytics Platform

1. Problem Statement

Satellite-based oceanographic datasets provide valuable information about changing marine environments. However, accessing, processing, and interpreting these datasets requires specialized scientific knowledge and technical tools.

Existing environmental platforms often lack sufficiently localized coastal analysis and clear explanations of data reliability.

Key challenges include:

  • Difficulty accessing historical satellite oceanographic data.
  • Limited location-specific coastal environmental information.
  • Challenges identifying seasonal variations and temperature anomalies.
  • Land contamination and mixed pixels affecting nearshore analysis.
  • Difficulty interpreting statistical trends and uncertainty.
  • Confusion between historical observations, trends, and actual forecasts.

SEA//SAFE addresses these challenges through an integrated platform combining satellite data, geospatial processing, scientific analytics, and interactive visualization.

2. Project Objectives

  1. Integrate NASA/JPL MUR SST v4.1 through NASA Earthdata and PO.DAAC.
  2. Automate historical data acquisition, spatial subsetting, and storage.
  3. Generate coastal marine analysis regions using geospatial processing.
  4. Create offshore sensitivity zones at 5 km, 10 km, and 20 km.
  5. Calculate monthly and seasonal SST averages.
  6. Identify temperature anomalies using a documented climatological baseline.
  7. Evaluate long-term temperature trends using statistical methods.
  8. Visualize results through interactive maps and dashboards.
  9. Communicate data provenance, coverage, confidence, and uncertainty.
  10. Support reproducible analysis and downloadable reports.

3. How SEA//SAFE Works

The platform follows five stages.

3.1 Location Selection

Users select coastal locations through an interactive map, manual search, or optional browser geolocation. Coordinates are validated against the pilot coastal region.

3.2 Historical Ocean Data Exploration

The system retrieves and processes historical SST data to display daily observations, monthly and seasonal averages, temperature variations, anomalies, and data coverage.

3.3 Geospatial Coastal Analysis

Three offshore analysis zones are generated:

  • 5 km coastal buffer.
  • 10 km coastal buffer.
  • 20 km coastal buffer.

Land and unsuitable mixed coastal pixels are excluded or flagged to improve marine analysis reliability.

3.4 Statistical Trend Analysis

Historical temperature changes are evaluated using:

  • Ordinary Least Squares (OLS).
  • Theil–Sen slope estimation.
  • Mann–Kendall trend testing.
  • Seasonal Mann–Kendall testing where appropriate.
  • 95% confidence intervals.
  • Autocorrelation assessment.

Results include trend direction, statistical significance, and uncertainty.

3.5 Forecast and Environmental Outlook

The platform displays documented operational forecasts or independently validated model outputs when available. Otherwise, it displays:

"No validated predictive model available for this coastal location."

Historical trends are never presented as validated forecasts.

4. NASA Earth Observation Data

Primary Dataset: NASA/JPL Multi-scale Ultra-high Resolution Sea Surface Temperature (MUR SST v4.1).

Supporting NASA Resources

  • NASA Earthdata Search – Dataset discovery.
  • NASA Earthdata Login – Authentication.
  • NASA PO.DAAC – Oceanographic data access.
  • NASA Harmony – Data subsetting.
  • NASA Worldview – Satellite visualization.
  • NASA Giovanni – Scientific data exploration.

Proposed Data Processing Pipeline

  1. Authenticate through NASA Earthdata.
  2. Retrieve MUR SST data.
  3. Subset the Thiruvananthapuram coastal region.
  4. Validate NetCDF files and inspect metadata.
  5. Apply quality checks and land/sea masking.
  6. Convert Kelvin to Celsius after verifying units.
  7. Aggregate daily observations into monthly and seasonal averages.
  8. Calculate climatology and SST anomalies.
  9. Perform statistical trend analysis.
  10. Store processed data for API access and visualization.

5. Scientific Methodology

5.1 Temperature Conversion

MUR SST values are commonly stored in Kelvin.

[
T(°C)=T(K)-273.15
]

Conversion must be performed exactly once after verifying the variable metadata.

5.2 Climatology

The proposed reference period is 2003–2020. Monthly climatological baselines are calculated using the average temperature for each calendar month across the reference years.

5.3 SST Anomalies

[
Anomaly=Observed\ SST-Monthly\ Baseline
]

Positive anomalies indicate temperatures above the baseline; negative anomalies indicate temperatures below it.

5.4 Trend Analysis

OLS provides a preliminary trend estimate, while Theil–Sen and Mann–Kendall methods support robust trend assessment.

Statistical outputs include:

  • Trend slope in °C/year and °C/decade.
  • Trend direction.
  • 95% confidence interval.
  • Mann–Kendall p-value.
  • Autocorrelation assessment.
  • Analysis period and methodology.

All reported results must be calculated from validated data, not illustrative examples.

7. System Architecture and Developer Responsibilities

The project is divided into six development modules.

Developer 1 – NASA Data Pipeline & Ingestion Engineer

Focus: Data acquisition and ETL.

  • NASA Earthdata authentication.
  • MUR SST v4.1 integration.
  • Automated historical data extraction.
  • Spatial and temporal subsetting.
  • NetCDF/Zarr storage.
  • Data validation and offline fallback.

Deliverables: Authentication modules, automated downloader, validation scripts, and offline sample datasets.

Developer 2 – Ocean Analytics & Scientific Compute Engineer

Focus: Scientific computation and statistical analysis.

  • Daily-to-monthly aggregation.
  • Seasonal averages and climatology.
  • SST anomaly calculations.
  • Theil–Sen trend estimation.
  • Mann–Kendall significance testing.
  • Confidence intervals and autocorrelation assessment.
  • Forecast availability handling.

Deliverables: Analytics modules, statistical functions, and reproducible Jupyter notebooks.

Developer 3 – Geospatial & Boundary Processing Engineer

Focus: Coastal geography and spatial validation.

  • Administrative boundary acquisition.
  • Coastline processing.
  • 5 km, 10 km, and 20 km offshore buffers.
  • Land/sea raster masking.
  • Mixed coastal pixel handling.
  • Coordinate validation.

Deliverables: GeoJSON boundaries, offshore buffer layers, and Boolean ocean masks.

Developer 4 – Backend API & Data Service Engineer

Focus: API development and infrastructure.

  • FastAPI application and REST endpoints.
  • PostgreSQL/PostGIS integration.
  • Analytical result caching.
  • CSV export services.
  • Docker containerization.
  • Data provenance and metadata services.

Deliverables: Backend application, API routes, schemas, database integration, and Docker configuration.

Developer 5 – Frontend Core & User Experience Developer

Focus: Application architecture and user experience.

  • Next.js application structure.
  • Responsive dark ocean-themed interface.
  • Navigation and reusable UI components.
  • Location search and browser geolocation.
  • Global state management.
  • Data provenance panel.
  • Safety disclaimer and advisory links.

Deliverables: Application pages, location selection, reusable components, and metadata interface.

Developer 6 – Frontend Geospatial & Data Visualization Developer

Focus: Interactive mapping and analytical visualization.

  • MapLibre coastline integration.
  • Offshore buffer visualization.
  • Interactive map selection.
  • Historical SST charts.
  • SST anomaly visualization.
  • Trend and confidence interval cards.
  • Forecast status panel.
  • CSV download integration.

Deliverables: Coastal map, analytical charts, trend cards, forecast panel, and visualization components.

9. Expected Impact

SEA//SAFE aims to improve access to localized oceanographic information for:

  • Coastal and fishing communities.
  • Oceanography and environmental researchers.
  • Students and educational institutions.
  • Environmental organizations.
  • Coastal planners and policymakers.

Potential applications include environmental awareness, regional climate research, coastal observation, educational activities, and evidence-based environmental planning.

10. Future Scope

After establishing a reliable SST analysis framework, the platform may expand to:

  • Ocean colour and chlorophyll-a.
  • Rainfall and precipitation.
  • Sea-level anomalies.
  • Wind conditions.
  • Ocean waves and currents.
  • Multi-dataset SST comparison.
  • Spatial trend mapping.
  • Additional Kerala coastal regions.
  • Validated operational forecast integration.
  • Advanced predictive modelling.
  • Downloadable scientific reports.

11. Scientific Limitations and Safety

SEA//SAFE is an environmental information and decision-support platform, not an official marine weather warning, fishing advisory, cyclone prediction, or emergency response system.

MUR SST v4.1 is a Level 4 analysed product rather than direct satellite measurements at every grid cell. Coastal resolution, land contamination, missing observations, temporal coverage, and product uncertainty must be considered.

All findings must include their analysis period, methods, limitations, and confidence.

Forecasts will only be presented when supported by an appropriate operational source or independently validated predictive model.

12. Project Vision

SEA//SAFE aims to bridge the gap between complex satellite-based oceanographic data and the people who need understandable information about their coastal environment.

By combining NASA Earth observation, scientific computing, geospatial intelligence, and modern web technologies, the platform seeks to make coastal environmental changes easier to explore, interpret, and communicate.

SEA//SAFE — See the change. Understand the ocean. Prepare for what comes next.
